principle_text: When the conversation is focused on personal background and rapport building, avoid delaying introduction of the charitable cause to maintain relevance and guide toward donation discussion.
When the persuadee responds with related small talk questions, avoid focusing solely on casual information that does not guide the conversation toward the donation goal.
When the persuadee shows casual interest without commitment, avoid merely stating facts or asking yes/no questions that do not deepen engagement or move toward donation.
When the persuadee responds with neutral or unrelated information, avoid asking questions that do not connect to the charitable cause or donation goal.
When the persuadee shows openness and positive feelings toward a cause, you should ask direct questions about donation amounts to encourage commitment and clarify their willingness to give.
When the persuadee responds with neutral or minimal engagement, avoid making casual remarks that do not connect to the donation appeal or advance the charitable conversation.
When the persuadee responds with neutral agreement to casual small talk, avoid focusing solely on unrelated topics that do not guide the conversation toward the donation goal.
When the persuadee responds with vague or non-committal remarks, avoid assuming understanding or interest without further clarification or engagement.
When the persuadee responds neutrally to personal small talk unrelated to the cause, avoid shifting focus away from the charity or donation appeal.
When the persuadee shows awareness of the charity, you should engage their interest by inviting them to learn more details to deepen their involvement.
When the persuadee shows interest in personal details, avoid giving minimal or unrelated responses that do not build rapport or guide the conversation toward the donation goal.
When the persuadee shows basic awareness of the charity without expressing commitment, avoid asking only about their knowledge without linking it to the impact or benefits of donating.
When the persuadee shares personal challenges unrelated to the cause, avoid asking unrelated detailed questions that do not connect to the charitable donation goal.
When the persuadee shows only basic awareness of a charity without engagement, avoid asking neutral questions that do not encourage deeper connection or commitment to the cause.
When the persuadee shows familiarity and prior support for a charity, you should acknowledge their involvement to build rapport and encourage deeper engagement.
When the persuadee shows only vague or minimal knowledge about the charity, avoid asking closed questions that elicit neutral acknowledgments without encouraging deeper engagement or commitment.
